name: Adam Khan Chapli Kabob
subtitle: Eastern Afghanistan’s famous chapli kabob culture, best paired with fresh sugar cane juice.
card_description: Adam Khan in Jalalabad is known for larger-than-life chapli kabob patties prepared in front of guests.

name: Kunar Trout
subtitle: Fresh river fish, mountain water, roadside grills, and the scenery of eastern Afghanistan.
card_description: Pair Kunar’s river valleys with grilled trout, tandoor naan, and one of Afghanistan’s most scenic food experiences.

name: Kandahari Rosh
subtitle: Slow-cooked Kandahari rosh as a southern hospitality experience.
card_description: Taste Kandahar’s slow-cooked lamb tradition as part of a southern Afghanistan journey.

name: Chashma-e-Dogh
subtitle: A beloved Kabul gathering place built around chilled dogh, families, pilgrims, and local life.
card_description: Visit Chashma-e-Dogh for dogh, local snacks, family atmosphere, and a natural pairing with Istalif or western Kabul routes.

name: Traditional Chainaki in Kabul
subtitle: Teapot-stew hospitality and everyday Kabul dining culture.
card_description: Experience chainaki — meat slow-cooked in a teapot — as a classic Kabul comfort-food tradition.

name: Aziz Bakery
subtitle: Cakes, cookies, crème rolls, and Kabul celebration sweets in the heart of Chicken Street.
card_description: Stop at Aziz Bakery for Afghan cakes, cookies, crème rolls, and the sweets that families carry to visits and celebrations.

name: Bamyan Kabob
subtitle: Highland kabob culture in Bamyan’s mountain setting.
card_description: Share kabob, bread, and highland hospitality as part of a Bamyan stay.

name: Band-e-Amir Dairy Market & Quroot
subtitle: Roadside dairy markets between Bamyan and Band-e-Amir, famous for dried yogurt.
card_description: Stop along the Bamyan–Band-e-Amir road for quroot, local dairy, highland humor, and a taste visitors never forget.

name: Arg Restaurant — Herat
subtitle: A grand Herat dining experience after the citadel, bazaars, glass workshops, and saffron tea.
card_description: End a Herat day with a memorable Afghan feast at Arg Restaurant, one of the city’s strongest hospitality experiences.

name: Ghazni Palaw
subtitle: Palaw hospitality in historic Ghazni.
card_description: Taste rice hospitality and shared-table dining as part of a Ghazni stop.

name: Mansoor Kabob
subtitle: Northern kabob hospitality linked to the Mazar–Balkh travel corridor.
card_description: A northern kabob stop travelers use when exploring Mazar-e-Sharif and the Balkh corridor.
